raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Literal stop-string selection depends on configured list order when speculative
decoding accepts multiple tokens. For stop `["XY", "STOP"]` and a chunk decoding
to `kSTOPXY`, the current code selects `XY` and emits `kSTOP`, while one-token
steps stop at `STOP` and emit `k`.

## Modifications

Choose the matching literal stop with the earliest token-completion boundary,
using the existing bounded locator. Keep configured list priority when multiple
stops first appear in the same token. Preserve one-token short-circuit behavior,
decoded-text fallback, regex selection, and EOS/grammar/length priority.

The existing CPU regression file compares chunked and sequential completion,
finished lengths, token IDs through the stop, and actual detokenizer trimming.
It also guards same-token ties and a single decode on the one-token path.

## Accuracy Tests

- Final base: `ce617d410bce1a9db48bbada8ee97a1286729e84`
- Final regressions fail in four subtests on unchanged production code and pass
  with the fix
- Six related CPU test files: 118 passed, 30 subtests passed
- 25,216 deterministic additive-tokenizer cases: 802 mismatches before, zero after
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed, including Rust hooks
- Whole-manager collection has the same two baseline environment blockers:
  missing `parameterized` and HiSparse requiring an accelerator

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No GPU or performance claim. Multi-token matching can run the bounded locator
once per matching stop candidate, causing additional prefix decodes. Single-token
matching still decodes once.
Existing decode-window/context-sensitive-tokenizer limitations are unchanged.

## Related scope

Inspected #33045 (length/stop priority), #41522 (decoded-text fallback removal),
#36728 (window sizing), and #41115 (tail memoization). None corrects this selection
loop. #33045 and #41522 touch nearby code and may need merge coordination.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with full-repository pre-commit hooks
- [x] Add CPU regressions in the existing registered test file
- [x] Follow existing code and test conventions
- Documentation: no public API change
- GPU inference and performance benchmarks: not run; limits are stated above

Codex assisted with implementation and testing.

+    def test_multiple_stop_strs_match_sequential_token_boundary(self):
+        # A later-listed stop can complete before the first-listed stop within
+        # one accepted chunk. Selection must match one-token-at-a-time decoding.
+        cases = [
+            ([], [10, STOP_ID, 70, 71], ["XY", "STOP"], "STOP", 2, "k"),
+            ([10, 70], [71, STOP_ID, 11], ["STOP", "XY"], "XY", 3, "k"),
+            ([], [10, STOP_ID, 70, 71], ["STOPXY", "STOP"], "STOP", 2, "k"),
+        ]
+        manager = DetokenizerManager.__new__(DetokenizerManager)
+        for prefix, chunk, stops, matched, finished_len, text in cases:
+            for stop_order in (stops, stops[::-1]):
+                with self.subTest(prefix=prefix, chunk=chunk, stops=stop_order):
+                    req = _make_req(prefix + chunk, stop=stop_order)
+                    req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=len(chunk))
+                    sequential = _make_req(prefix, stop=stop_order)
+                    for token in chunk:
+                        sequential.output_ids.append(token)
+                        sequential.update_finish_state()
+                        if sequential.finished():
+                            break
+
+                    self.assertTrue(req.finished())
+                    self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, matched)
+                    self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, finished_len)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        req.finished_reason.to_json(),
+                        sequential.finished_reason.to_json(),
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, sequential.finished_len)
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        req.output_ids_through_stop, sequential.output_ids_through_stop
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids), prefix + chunk)
+                    for no_stop_trim in (False, True):
+                        self.assertEqual(
+                            manager.trim_matched_stop(
+                                req.tokenizer.decode(req.output_ids_through_stop),
+                                req.finished_reason.to_json(),
+                                no_stop_trim,
+                            ),
+                            text + matched if no_stop_trim else text,
+                        )
+
+    def test_stop_strs_completing_in_same_token_keep_list_priority(self):
+        # Both strings appear in the STOP token. Character position must not
+        # override list priority when the first matching token is the same.
+        for stop_order in (["OP", "ST"], ["ST", "OP"]):
+            for chunk in ([STOP_ID], [STOP_ID, 70, 71]):
+                with self.subTest(stops=stop_order, chunk=chunk):
+                    req = _make_req([10] + chunk, stop=stop_order)
+                    req.update_finish_state(new_accepted_len=len(chunk))
+                    self.assertEqual(req.finished_reason.matched, stop_order[0])
+                    self.assertEqual(req.finished_len, 2)
+                    self.assertEqual(list(req.output_ids_through_stop), [10, STOP_ID])
